stories.headline: Nabers Is Off the Sick Wagon and Cuttin' Again in Jersey
stories.read: Nine of the Giants' first ten practices, pardner, and the man tore a knee clean apart last October. Malik Nabers is running routes, planting, and cutting with no limp in sight, and the outfit in East Rutherford is quietly pointing at Week 1 against Dallas. Here's the play: half the saloon is still too spooked to grab him, so his price has slid a full round or two below where a fella with his cut of the throws belongs. That's the vein, and it's sitting right out in the open. Stake it before the herd notices he's healthy.

stories.headline: Luther Burden Pulls Up Lame in Chicago, and the Whole Bears Camp Shifts
stories.read: Burden got tangled up with a corner on a contested grab in red-zone drills Saturday and came away with a groin strain, and the word out of Halas Hall is he misses the entire preseason. The good news is the Bears still expect him saddled up for the opener in Carolina on September 13, so this ain't a funeral. But a second-year fella who needed camp reps to lock down his share of the throws just lost every one of 'em, and the price on him is about to drop while the nervous folks bail. If you got the bench to be patient, that dip is cheap gold. If you need points in September, let somebody else hold the bag.

stories.headline: Pacheco Tweaks a Knee in Detroit, and the Spare Horse Talk Gets Loud
stories.read: Dan Campbell stepped out Monday and called it a little MCL sprain, nothing that keeps Isiah Pacheco out of the opener against New Orleans. Doc believes him, mostly, but note what else came out of that same ranch: starting center Cade Mays is laid up eight to ten weeks with a busted wrist, and that's the fella who opens the lanes. So Jahmyr Gibbs stays the bell cow and nothing changes at the top, but the spare horse behind him just got a question mark stapled to his saddle. If you drafted Gibbs, you needed Pacheco anyway. Grab him a round later than you planned and thank Doc in December.
